IBM.rationale: IBM presents a mixed but mildly attractive picture. On the positive side, Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +9.5%, EPS +14.3%), with Software growing 11% and Infrastructure +15% driven by the z17 mainframe super-cycle. The company has a $12.5B cumulative generative AI bookings pipeline, record FY2025 FCF of $14.7B, and a 31-year dividend growth streak. ROE has improved to 32.5% and net margin to 15.6%. However, several concerns temper enthusiasm: (1) QoQ metrics show significant sequential deceleration (revenue -6.2%, EPS -44.6%), suggesting the Q2 2025 quarter was an outlier; (2) the stock has already corrected ~22% from its June 2 all-time high of $332.46 to $258.27, partly reflecting disappointment that full-year guidance was merely 'above 5%' growth; (3) consulting growth is weak at ~1% growth, and Accenture's recent guidance cut signalsates sector headwinds; (4) the PE ratio compressed from ~50x to ~23x, which is now near the low end of its 1-year range (19-51), suggesting some valuation reset has occurred but not yet at distressed levels. The quantum computing tailwinds from executive orders and CHIPS Act funding are longer-term positives but not near-term earnings drivers. Q2 2026 earnings in late July could be a catalyst if Software growth reaccelerates. Net: solid franchise with improving fundamentals, valuation now more reasonable after correction, but consulting weakness and mainframe cycle peak risk cap the upside.
